utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I was informed that the Prosecution would like to raise some matters, and before I give an opportunity to do so, my first question would be whether the invitation to upload a redacted version of the Croatian Helsinki Committee report because which was tendered through witness W140 whether that has been uploaded already because there were submissions made in relation to that report. But one of the first issues was whether it did not also deal with matters which are totally outside the scope of this indictment. So whatever the Chamber will decide on the matter, and I see Ms. Higgins is not there this morning, but whatever we'll decide, at least the Chamber invited the Prosecution to limit the report to what is maybe relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I have been informed that the redacted version is ready. We sent it to the Defence to see if there was any objections, so I think we're waiting for a response before uploading it into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's at least good that it has been done. When did you send it to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't have that information off the top of my head. But I think at least a week ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is the case, Mr. Cayley is there any way that you inquire perhaps Ms. Higgins --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour, and see. I'm quite certain -- I'm actually just told she is in the process of reviewing it now. So we can certainly get back to the Court in short order. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because perhaps later this morning, we might deal with quite a lot of issues from the MFI list. Thank you for that information. Mr. Hedaraly, you wanted to raise it a matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I wanted to raise an issue with respect to 1D69-0104. Perhaps we can have is on the screen so that everyone can refer to it at the same time. And that is the list of targets. If you remember, Mr. President, yesterday Mr. Misetic at transcript reference 16980 without putting any questions to the witness, showed that document, said it was a list of targets and then asked to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the list with the many stacionars on it --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and the houses where they apparently were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: First of all, that should have been a bar table submission and the proper procedure was not followed. That is not the main issues that we have with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You referred to it as 1D69-0104. But I remember that a --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No number was given to it in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No numbers given to in the transcript. Then we failed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We can give one now if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that -- Mr. Registrar, this target list since it is on our screen, apart from -- so an MFI number for the time being would do, I would say, waiting for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it gets a D number. That's -- it was introduced by the Gotovina Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D1447, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps if we can have the Croatian version on the screen it may assist for the first set of issues that the Prosecution has with this document. And, Mr. President, the first issue is that there is absolutely no indication of where this document was created, by whom, there was a date at the bottom saying 30 July. But as far as we know it could just have been typed up by anyone. On its face there is no indicia of authenticity and, therefore, no reliability. In fact, the document itself has a list on the left-hand column of targets, and there are significant numbers that have been skipped. For example, 87 to 273, 361 to 491, 564 to 615, 794 to 917; and in some instances there are also coordinates missing. In some instances under source of information in the English it says "old one," so the Prosecution has no way of knowing what this document is. It has just been tendered and presented for -- presumably what is a list of targets for -- for TS-3 at the time, which, raises the next issue we have with this. Is that on its very face of the document, we know from the evidence in this case so far that it was TS-5 that fired on the town of Benkovac, for example. Now, there is evidence of a reorganisation that was made and that is what Mr. Rajcic testified to. But that's precisely the point, Your Honour. Mr. Rajcic testified to the targets in Benkovac, in Obrovac, in Gracac. His 92 ter statement he said he, himself, prepared the artillery attack. Mr. Russo asked Mr. Rajcic -- May I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I heard some sounds or noise, and I didn't know where it came from. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Rajcic was asked specifically to identify the targets on a map of Benkovac, of Gracac, and of Obrovac. And now the Defence is -- didn't put that document to Mr. Rajcic despite the fact that there are now targets that appear on their presentation, targets that appear on this list that were not mentioned by Mr. Rajcic. Now, Your Honour, under Rule 90 (H) the Defence had an obligation to put their case to Mr. Rajcic, and the Prosecution asked specific questions on that the targeting and the targets in those towns; and that list was not put in cross-examination to Mr. Rajcic. So the two issues here from the face of it, the authenticity of the document, and the person that can testify to this authenticity is not Mr. Sinobad, it is Mr. Rajcic. So instead of just putting this within nine transcript lines at page 16980, without a single question to the witness, asked it to be tendered into evidence for the last witness when it was done, not done with Mr. Rajcic was there, is improper. If this exhibit gets into evidence, the Prosecution would like to recall Mr. Rajcic and ask him about this document and his knowledge of it to see whether we can actually authenticate it because there is no basis right now to know. There's no stamp. There's nothing on this document from the face of it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hedaraly, first of all, one question, you said the Prosecution was under an obligation to put its case to Mr. Rajcic. Now that is only evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Defence, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Isn't it true that if you -- that's not a general rule, that in cross-examination you should put your case to a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is true, Your Honour. But when there is an issue where the witness that is the most familiar with it and has testified to it, there is a document that he could perhaps authenticate that he has discussed more or less the substance of that testimony; and Defence doesn't put that document to the witness and then tries to essentially bar table it or show it to a witness where it's acknowledged in the transcript, You've probably never seen this document before, and then tried to tender, that is clearly improper and the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you read a reference to Rule 90 and to Rule 90 (H). What appears to be the criterion there is if you go beyond the limits of the subject matter of examination-in-chief that then you are under an obligation to put the nature of your case to that witness; so, therefore, we still have to see whether that is -- was the case or not here. But that's at least what I read in Rule 90 (H).

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if -- that -- that may be true. If what the Defence is saying now is that there are targets in Benkovac, for example; there also Gracac and Obrovac on that list by the way. If the Defence is now saying there are other targets that the one -- that were identified by the -- by Mr. Rajcic, and the Defence didn't put that document to him then, then the Prosecution should be entitled to recall Mr. Rajcic and put this document to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- we'll consider whether this would justify a recall of Mr. Rajcic. Let's first listen to the -- Mr. Misetic, because he might tell us a bit about the background and the origin of this document and missing portions in the listing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me just start by saying that it with all due respect to the Prosecution it appears to me that they, on the last day of the Prosecution's case, still don't understand how artillery works or what Mr. Rajcic's testimony was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's focus on -- I mean this is kind of sweeping statements that they do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They really do not assist very much, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think I should wait for Mr. Russo to listen to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, there was a sweeping statement that the Prosecution does not understand artillery at all. I'm exaggerating a bit, but that was the opening line of Mr. Misetic, who is now going to tell us about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That is my closing argument, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's closing argument. It was your opening sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, what Mr. Rajcic testified to what targets were fired on on Benkovac on 4th August; that is far different from saying what planned targets are or what you put on a target list. Mr. Rajcic addressed that distinction in his Rule 92 ter statement, so the fact that you have a list of dozens if not hundreds of targets that were not fired on has nothing to do with Mr. Rajcic's testimony or what was put to him by the Prosecution; nor is it in any way inconsistent with what Mr. Rajcic said. It is a fact that Mr. Rajcic said - and we put those circles in our presentation yesterday - that three targets were fired upon; that doesn't mean in artillery preparation that you don't put together a list of potential targets, and this is what this list purports to be. Secondly, the source of the document is well known to the Prosecution. They have filed a document with the Trial Chamber already about this document. This is the motion filed by the Prosecution on 21 January 2009. This is the motion seeking production of documents obtained by Gotovina Defence at Annex A, paragraph 12. The Prosecution says and this is now a document concerning Mr. Ivanovic and the indictment in Zagreb. The Prosecution said that that indictment covers two documents; one described as a code map of targets for the Benkovac-Obrovac-Gracac area, which is this document. The Prosecution further went on to advise the Trial Chamber that, thus, even if the Prosecution of Ivanovic proceeds and is successful, it could only result in the production of these two documents, neither of which appear to fall directly within the Prosecution's artillery document request. So, the -- and secondly, I can tell you, and Mr. Kehoe will also tell that you, we had a meeting with Mr. Russo, Mr. Tieger, and Mr. Waespi on the, I believe, the 12th of December last year where we also advised them that we had Mr. Kardum's diary as well as this, what the Prosecution referred to as code map of targets for the Benkovac-Obrovac-Gracac area; and it one of the documents given to us by Mr. Kardum, a copy. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, I haven't re-read the motion this morning, so there's something in my memory which tells me that talking about two documents, apparently the documents which were at stake in the investigations or at least in proceedings against Mr. Ivanovic, something in my mind tells me that in one or two submissions I read one of them we do not have and the other one we do have. But that's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you told the Prosecution that two documents were in your possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct, orally. We will told them at a meeting on the 12th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this in any way also -- has this put on the record in this court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we are not aware of it until now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but we now our. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, to the extent that Mr. Ivanovic has been indicted for the document and to the extent that the Prosecution has already written to the Chamber that this is a document that doesn't fall within the Prosecution's RFA, the Trial Chamber has some knowledge of the document that we're talking about now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Additionally, let me further state that Mr. Rajcic was clear in his testimony of the distinction between firing at the operational level and firing at the tactical level. This is Mr. Kardum's list of targets as of 30 July 1995. The gaps and the only way I can respond to this is in effect by providing my own testimony. The gaps are because this is a computer printout and the targets are related to the three cities, whereas, as I'm told the gaps refer to other locations and other targets. But this is the only copy that we have of this. The indication by Mr. Hedaraly that there is no stamp also goes to the issue that this is not an official document of the Republic of Croatia. And with respect to authentication and not putting documents to a witness that come, first of all, this document is something that was not at the operational level but was prepared by Mr. Kardum; so I'm not sure what it is that the Prosecution thinks they would put to him. Secondly, if that's the new standard that the Prosecution wishes to apply, then we would have to go back and seek to exclude all documents that the Prosecution tendered after their own witnesses came. To my mind, Mr. Marti comes to mind where documents and spreadsheets of bodies found after Mr. Marti left were then subsequently tendered across the bar table. One of the objections that we raised precisely was the fact that we couldn't put it to Mr. Marti. The Prosecution had no problem. So we would then go back and ask that the same rule be applied if that's the new rule that the Prosecution wishes to apply across the board. With respect to authenticity, it is what it purports to be. It's titled TS-3 as Mr. Hedaraly alluded to. The numbering for these artillery and rocket groups did not change until after the 1st of August, so the fact that it is called TS-3 is actually an indicia of reliability because if it was created after the fact, it was more likely that somebody would have put a mistake on there and called it TS-5, which in fact as of 30 July 1995, it wasn't called TS-5, it was called TS-3. That's also verified by Mr. Rajcic's testimony. Accordingly, Mr. President, I don't think these argument, and we can go on and on about reliability, credibility, et cetera; but that doesn't have anything to do with the admissibility of this document. It is what it purports to be, and if the Prosecution wishes to challenge the weight of this document at some point, they're free to do so, obviously; but in terms whether it should be admitted as I said, the Prosecution has been on notice at least as of the 1st of December of the existence of this document, and as of the 21st, I believe, of January, advise the Trial Chamber that this was not a document that they were looking for. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So now we have Mr. Misetic testifying extensively about there document. If to the extent that it relates to Mr. Rajcic's testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- I asked Mr. Misetic to refrain from sweeping statements. If would you do the same, then we could focus on the subject matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: With respect to Mr. Rajcic's testimony if I can give the floor to Mr. Russo since he examined the witness, he will be able to examine specifically what Mr. Rajcic did and did not testify to, if that is allowed by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, the Chamber know what is Mr. Rajcic's testified to. But I give an opportunity to Mr. Russo to draw our attention and to take us back to relevant portions of the testimony of Mr. Rajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before addressing the issues raised during Mr. Rajcic's testimony, I do want to clear up what I believe are inaccuracies in the statements just made by Mr. Misetic. First of all, this document that's in front of us the Prosecution is not or was not well aware of what this document is, nor that Mr. Misetic was going to claim that it was one of the documents given to his Defence team by Mr. Kardum. Now we did have a discussion with Mr. Misetic and Mr. Kehoe on the 11th of December, and during that conversation we were told by them that there were two documents given to the Defence team by Mr. Kardum. Those documents were not identified by title. The title of the document, code map of Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac comes from Mr. Kardum himself and comes from the indictment of Mr. Ivanovic and that's the reason why in our motion to compel documents from the Defence, confidential Appendix A, paragraph 12 we indicate that these documents do not, quote, appear to fall within our document request. Because our document request was not for code maps. Of course, this document is, first of all, not a code map. It's neither a map nor a coded map. It is quite plainly a list of targets. If it had been identified as by its title, list of targets for TS-3, it certainly falls within our document request and certainly falls within what we've been seeking in Rule 54 bis proceedings. So we were unaware that this was the document which was being referred to by Mr. Kardum as a code map, and in any case I don't see how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But this is what I do understand - and sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Russo - is that Mr. Misetic is blaming you for not understanding the matters that you say well, but this is not what we understood. It certainly falls within ... at least now you have got one document you would like to have at your disposal, and it's even tendered now into evidence by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, that might be the case. However, we simply, with all due respect, can't take Mr. Misetic's word that this document is what it purports to be, that it is, in fact, a source list of targets for TS-3 for whatever level of artillery, the only witness to appear in this case who could have provided that information was here to testify last week. In fact, the individual who planned the artillery attack on Benkovac-Obrovac-Gracac, the fact that it was not even shown to him so that the Chamber and the Prosecution could determine if, in fact, it is what it purports to be, then there simply no foundation for the document to come into evidence. We don't know that it, in fact, is a list of targets. Mr. Hedaraly has already pointed out the problems that appear from the face of the document. It certainly is something that needs information at a minimum as to whether it was the source list of targets used by TS-5, whether it was, in fact, used during Operation Storm, otherwise it is not relevant. And Mr. Sinobad obviously can't provide that information; so we simply can't do this by a vow of counsel. It needs to be put to a witness who can provide that information to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is it, with all due respect, his - almost his entire direct examination was put in documents to Mr. Rajcic, that Mr. Rajcic was not personally familiar. That's the first point; that he did not author, that did he not use the 4th Guards Brigade, the 7th Guards Brigade, the coded maps of the 7th Guards Brigade; none of those documents Mr. Rajcic had any personal knowledge of. So to now come back and say we have to put this document to him because he may or may not have personal knowledge of the document is defeated by what he did through his whole direct examination; and if necessary, Mr. President, we'll go back and put together a spreadsheet for you of all document that they have tendered or are trying to tender into evidence or bar table through Mr. Rajcic for which Mr. Rajcic has no personal knowledge. And if is that's the standard Mr. Russo wishes apply then we will move out all those documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me just make an additional point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, isn't it to some extend also not speculation to say he didn't know of all these documents, so he would not known about this one as well. We just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm saying you can't use a sword and a shield in the same argument, which is what Mr. Russo is doing. Let's get to the more fundamental point. Mr. Russo now claims if, in fact, we have to know whether the list was used during Operation Storm otherwise it's not relevant. That's completely false and completely counter to what our position is in light of the emphasis that Mr. Russo put on the meeting on the 31st of July at Brioni. The fact that there's a target list on the 30th of July, for the towns of Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac; and in an extensive target list whether or not it was used in Operation Storm this document has relevance in light of the Prosecution's theory of the case. So this document, Mr. President, should come in. They can argue the weight. And let me also say that we are more than willing to go back and look at all documents that the Prosecution has tendered into evidence for which no live witness was called. There have to be hundreds of such documents: Newspaper articles where nobody has been called that can authenticate or verify the authenticity; police interview notes for which neither of interviewee or the interviewer have been called to authenticate the documents. To say that this shouldn't come -- now this document shouldn't come into evidence because it can't be put to a witness or wasn't put to a witness is completely at odds with how the Prosecution has tendered evidence in this case. I suggest to you, Mr. President, that this is a list that is relevant to this witness in light of what the Prosecution put to him, and let me state that the Prosecution called this witness to testify about the shelling of Benkovac; and called him to say that what was shelled was residential areas; and called him to say there was only one military target in town, which was the barracks and there were no other targets. Accordingly, this is why this list was relevant with this witness it should come in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, let's try to finish this debate.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note could -- Your Honour, would you please kindly switch off your microphone. Would you please switch off your microphone, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the documents shown to Mr. Rajcic during his direct examination although he did not personally author many of them, they were, nevertheless, personally reviewed by him and, in fact, used by him to create the reports and documents which we tendered into evidence. So it is not a similar situation to what Mr. Misetic is describing. Irrespective of that, however, the fact that this list of targets is being offered, presumably to establish to the Court what the other targets were in Benkovac, or that there were targets in addition to those indicated by Mr. Rajcic, goes directly to Rule 90 (H) (ii). Essentially, they are saying Mr. Rajcic identified only four targets in and around the town of Benkovac. They're indicating with this target list there were in fact more targets than those four. Under Rule 90 (H) (ii) they were required to put that to Mr. Rajcic, to tell him, Well, isn't it true there were in fact more targets. Whether they were corps level artillery targets or brigade level targets is immaterial. The question I asked him, Mr. President, and this is it at page 16308, line 17 to 18, I asked him about the targets inside the town of Benkovac that were fired at by Croatian forces on either the 4th or 5th of August. Now Croatian forces, I specifically worded the question that way because that encompasses Croatian forces not simply the corps level artillery. I asked him to provide all of the targets. He provided only four. They're now indicating through this target list and putting on a map more targets which they didn't ask him about. Now we ask not ignore the fact that this was the witness who planned the attack on these towns. There has to be a reason why this list was not shown to Mr. Rajcic. If we had had it in our possession at the time, we certainly would have put it to him, asked him if it was accurate, asked him if it's the source list that he refers to for targets, ask him about the discrepancies in the document itself, any number of things. But, in any case, this document requires the testimony of at least some witness who can provide the information that Mr. Misetic is attempting to provide by a vow, which is that it was a target list which was either used in some fashion, referred to in some fashion by Croatian forces. None of that is apparent from the face of the document. For all we know this document was typed up by a third party who doesn't have anything to do with Operation Storm. There is simply no way to know without a witness testify to. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Misetic, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, Mr. Russo is inflating two separate issues. He cited to the transcript which is exact justifies our point. Mr. Russo asked Mr. Rajcic which targets were fired on, on the 4th. This list is not a list of targets fired on. It is a list of potential targets. It's dated the 30th of July. So obviously this list does not purport to list what was fired on, on the 4th of August. Therefore, he didn't put to Mr. Rajcic what were the potential targets in Benkovac. Secondly, with respect to the relevance of the material as I said there are at least several points here: One, was there a list of targets prior to the 31st of July for these towns? This document can help the Chamber assess that. Secondly, which we did for the Chamber, by the way, Mr. President, we plotted the coordinates on a map for the Chamber as they relate to what Mr. Rajcic testified what was actually fired on, and if the Court will recall yesterday, in the interests of candor with the Court it was us who pointed out there appears to be a discrepancy of about 150 metres on one of the targets. So there is some relevance here for the Chamber to know whether the Croatian army, prior to the 4th of August, had coordinates or targets that Mr. Rajcic identified as having been fired upon on the 4th of August. And finally, Mr. President, as I said, I'm willing to go back if -- if the Prosecution wishes that we do so, and go back and look at all of the evidence they have tendered that has not gone in through a live witness, which has been unable to be cross-examined. That's not the standard. I am not providing any testimony. The document is what it is. And I was asked by the Prosecution who provided it to us. The Prosecution itself has provided documents and tendered them into evidence, documents that were given to them by witnesses, which they moved into evidence. Mr. Roberts comes to mind. All sorts of documents he claims to have in a personal archive in Banja Luka which he brought to the Prosecution and they tendered into evidence. How do we know that Mr. Roberts didn't alter documents, create photographs, et cetera? These are all matters that can be argued, Mr. President, but they don't go to admissibility. One moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Mr. Kehoe calls to my attention the irony of the fact that we are going to probably at some point today be arguing about six -- five pages of bar table documents of Mr. Rajcic that were never put to him at all, that were not even put on the 65 ter list to be admitted. So there -- there does appear to be some discrepancy here. The Prosecution documents that they wish to put to the witness are suddenly -- can't come in unless they were put to the witness, but five pages of bar table documents they wish to put in were not put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The number is not irrelevant, but not certainly not a decisive issue. Let's try to remain focussed on ... The Chamber will decide on admission. That's -- Mr. Hedaraly, and may need some more time to do that after the exchange of views of today. Yes, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The only issue I would -- I would add to that is that obviously it would also relate to D1446 which was the presentation that was tendered with those numbers and, therefore, if the -- if this document that was MFI'd does not get in, the presentation to the extent it relates to those points should also not be in. On that note, Mr. President, there was another discrepancy -- that's a separate issue on the map, on D1446. If we go to page 12 of D1446, which is the wider map of Benkovac which some of the points plotted from the map. We see there are two additional targets that seem to be in the town of Benkovac that are 49 and 76. However, the coordinates for those two appear to be not near the town of Benkovac. In fact, one of them is in an infantry trench in Korune [phoen] in 49, but that appears to be right in the centre of Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. Hedaraly is confusing the grid coordinates on the map with the targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was what I would ask him. The numbers 46, we see that the grid coordinates in the area of the 70s and 80s and the 40s, 50s. So, therefore, I wonder whether that is not a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. That makes sense. But I just note that this list does not only include the three towns as Mr. Misetic mentioned but also points around the front line as we saw in the first pages of the presentation. The point is if the underlying list does not get in then this should also be excluded. That was the main point I wanted to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear. Mr. Misetic, one question, you explained to us the reasons why portions there was -- where the sequence of numbers could be explained by the entries being irrelevant for this case because it was a computer spreadsheet or at least were you -- gave an explanation and you related it to the existence of a spreadsheet of which only part was printed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me say, first of all, I'm being accused of testifying, so I'm doing this at the invitation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you a question -- I have not even asked you a question, as a matter of fact. I just have drawn your attention to an observation made by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As -- Mr. Hedaraly would say part of your testimony. I'm not saying that at this moment. You remember that you referred to this being a printout of part only.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's -- how do you know that and is there the complete spreadsheet still available, or -- apparently you have some knowledge about how this was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: All can I tell you, Mr. President, is again what I have been told. This is it a document not -- that was not printed out now. It was printed out in July of 1995. So it is not for this case that it was selected, the printout. I have been told through interviews of Mr. Kardum that when the target coordinates were sent out or printed by this TRS group that it -- what was selected was what was relevant for what the TRS group would be doing. They were givens the towns of Benkovac, Obrovac, and Gracac and to the extent that there are gaps, again, giving away proffer as to what I was told. Those gaps are because those gap do not deal with targets in the zone of responsibility of TRS-3. And your second question about whether the underlying documentation exists, that's obviously something that is in hot investigation at the moment. We don't have it, and we have not been told that such a master list either still exists, or if it does, where it might be located. We were given a hard copy printout, which is this, which I have been told was printed out in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And it was given to us by Mr. Kardum, which just for the record and if necessary we'll translate it, Mr. Kardum testified in Zagreb about a week ago. I have the -- it's not a transcript, it's a record by a record keeper where he also testified openly in public about the fact that he gave us this document as well as the Kardum diary. And Mr. Kehoe also correctly pointed out that I should correct Mr. Russo who said that at our meeting on the 11th of December we didn't talk about what the titles of documents were. We have a whole chain of e-mails from both Mr. Tieger and Mr. Russo asking for the Kardum diary. So obviously we did talk about what the substance of the documents was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, that's your submission in this -- The Chamber will consider the admission into evidence of this document. Are we ready to -- are we ready, I should say. Mr. Misetic, I should address you, are you ready to continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the examination of the witness. Then, Madam Usher, could you then please escort the witness into the courtroom. Could I meanwhile ask you, Mr. Misetic, at the risk of inviting you to give testimony, the grid references with five digits result in what area exactly covered by it? I mean the more digits there are, the smaller the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five digits would result in?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe the five digits take it down to a 50-metre square, 50-metre range, if I'm not mistaken. That may be one back down but it is significantly less. I do know that the -- I don't know if these -- these changes are necessarily arithmetic or geometric. I take it they must be geometric. They are not necessarily perfect. I do know that when you go from the 10th to the 100th that is a definitely a 100-metre square reduction. I don't know if we go to the thousands if it is equally true. And I don't want to mislead you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, it would be good to now how price --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will find that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- these grid references are, and to the extent you could agree on it with the Prosecution after some 50 minutes of debate that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just on the time-frame, there is one expert that I talked to about these grid-references, I just need to get him on the phone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not blaming you for -- and for anything at this moment. I only want to urge the parties to see to what extent they can inform the Chamber jointly rather than to have long debates about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sinobad. It is quite impolite to invite you in this courtroom and then to continue with discussions which we have started already. Apologies for that. And also apologies for the fact that you to wait for such a long time. Mr. Sinobad, I would like to remind you that the solemn declaration that you gave at the beginning of your testimony yesterday still bind you, and Mr. Misetic will now continue his cross-examination. Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sinobad.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar if we can pick up where we left off yesterday. If we could call up 1D00-0874, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let us start off where we left off yesterday and work our way backwards to see what we may have seen. If we go to -- this is again the statement of Djuro Vukasinovic, who I believe yesterday, you indicated is someone who worked in the police station. And if we go to paragraph 12 which is on page 4. Mr. Vukasinovic says at paragraph 12 that while he was meeting with local representatives at around 4.35 the shelling started again. A shell fell within two metres of the police station building, hitting the ticket office of the stadium that was next door to the police station and I asked you yesterday if you knew anything yesterday if you knew anything about a shell landing 2 metres from the police station. And you indicated you did not, can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can he tell us in what direction is the stadium from the police station: North, south, east, or west?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is to the right-hand side of the bus station. That's where the stadium is as well as the court building. Excuse me, the police station building. So that is to the right-hand side toward the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now if we could go back to page 2 of this document, paragraph 3. Mr. Vukasinovic told the Office of the Prosecutor when he woke up he went out on the balcony and could see clearly where the shells were coming from. He says: "I saw shells landing at the following locations: The petrol station, the fire brigade, where offices of civil protection and the Red Cross were and the Bagat on a Kepol factories. I could hear also that the shells were landing in the direction of the Benkovac barracks." Did you see any shells landing in the vicinity of the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear anything, save for the things I told you I saw that morning at Barice. That's the only thing I can confirm to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How many petrol stations were there in Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the petrol station was?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is at the intersection of the roads from Zadar and Biograd. From the fire brigade building, it is about 100 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me see if we can have you draw that on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we have 1D69-0102, please. Actually, it's not ... I think we need a better map. Mr. Registrar, if we could have D1446, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just -- if it assists we have a blank map that the witness marked in direct. It's 65 ter 5186. It may be easier than --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me see, I think I prefer the satellite view, but ... Could we go to the next page, please. Could we have page 9 of this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, with the assistance of the usher, are you able to circle the location of the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is in the part I encircled. It is at the cross-roads, one coming from Biograd and the other one from Zadar. There seems to be another stretch here, but I'm not sure whether it is the railway or something else. In any case, the part that I marked should reflect the area where the gas station is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the exhibit be marked and I tender only the page that [indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection to that page with the marking, pending, of course, the numbers on in this map being subject to the issues raised earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The numbers on this map I only see the grid references, 76, 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Then it is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do not see any targets here. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit D1448.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Registrar, if we could call up now 1D69-0091, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is now the issue of Barice being shelled, the residential area, which you testified about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... statement given by Mr. Bozidar Uzelac; do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there are several. In any case, I knew a Bozidar Uzelac who was a misdemeanour judge, if that's the person then I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It appears that this statement is, in fact, given by a magistrate, so it may be the same person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was he approximately 40 years old in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now at paragraph 2, he says: "On the 4th of August, 1995, I was living in an apartment located in the area of Barice in Benkovac city. At 5.00 a.m. I was in my apartment and I heard explosions nearby." And a few lines down, he says: "Shells did not fall near my building. However, I was informed that only 200 to 300 metres where I was, in the area of the primary and secondary school, shells were falling." Mr. Sinobad, in fact, the shells weren't landing in the residential area of Barice. They were landing several hundred metres from the residential area of Barice; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot confirm this, because, in the complex of buildings, there are four or five of the buildings which cover a certain area, and perpendicular to that was the building where I lived. When I got out of my building, I could see shells falling in front of those of four or five buildings. As far as I could recall, Uzelac lived in the back row of those building, not in the front row. As for what he says, that the shells were landing in the area of the primary and secondary school, I cannot confirm that, since I have no knowledge of any shells landing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Just one minute, Mr. Sinobad. In yesterday's transcript, which is unofficial, and I don't have the updated numbers at page 26, line 3, Mr. Hedaraly asked you about the shelling. He asked you: "Now in your statement you say you observed this when you were going to the office. Did you observe the actual impacts then or did you observe the result of the impact?" And your answer was --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, let me ... "When I was leaving the apartment towards the south, I could see the area and I could still see smoke, and I noticed pieces of shrapnel on the facade. There was still some smoke at the site of impact." Now when confronted with Mr. Uzelac's statement, you say, at line page 28, line 10: "When I got out of my building, I could see shells falling in front of those four or five buildings." Now, why, today, do you say you could see the shells falling, yet yesterday when Mr. Hedaraly asked that you question, you said what you saw was the smoke and shrapnels on the side of the building?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I used different terminology. In any case, I meant the same thing. I did not leave my building and go towards the south. I just wanted to say that the exit of my building faces the south, and I went towards the bus station which is to the west of my building. What I wanted to say is that I saw the smoke, meaning that the shell had landed immediately prior to that. Could I see the smoke right after the impact. So perhaps I wasn't putting things precisely. But I stand by what I said yesterday: I saw the smoke. As for the short interval of time, it is very difficult to notice the shell actually landing, unless you are facing directly the area where the shell is going to land.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Sinobad, let me ask you about there meeting with the mayor of Benkovac, which you say took place around -- or you got a call around 4.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, if we could go back to 1D69-0025, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is, again, Mr. Vukasinovic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 3 in the English, at paragraph 11. I'm sorry. I'm told that the actual number is 1D00-0874, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Vukasinovic at paragraph 11 says: "At around 4.15, I was visited by three of my friends: The municipal president in Benkovac, Dr. Stevo Vuksa; one was the president of the Executive Council, Radomir Ivanis; and another was a lawyer, Radomir Kuzet. They came to see me to organise the movement of the civilians from the vulnerable areas." If we go to paragraph 14, he says: "I returned to the municipal hall around 6.00 p.m. About ten people were at the meeting and assignments were given to each person to ensure that the evacuation was carried out in an orderly manner. The persons in attendance were the three representatives from the government, the manager of civil protection, a representative of the bus company, a representative from the petrol station, and other managers of companies who had trucks. At the meeting everyone had their assignments, and it was agreed how the evacuation was to be arranged." Now, you were present at this meeting that Mr. Vukasinovic describes as -- in fact, you are the representative of the bus company to whom he refers; correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall attending such a large meeting. In particular, Djuro Vukasinovic, I don't remember him because he was an important person. As I said, I was summoned after some four hours to come to the municipal building and said that the vehicles had to be prepared. I did attend the meeting although I didn't stay all the way to the end and what I can say with certainty is that Djuro Vukasinovic was not in attendance while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's go to a different statement then. Mr. Registrar, if could I have 1D69-0005, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the statement of Mr. Vuksa, the mayor of Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn the page, please, in English at paragraph 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to draw your attention to the fact that he also says: "Shells fell on the football ground and also on the Benkovac village which is a residential village on the edge of town. I went outside and saw shells falling by the refrigerator plant, the barracks, and the firemen's haul." If we could turn the page, please. Do you know what the firemen's hall was used for?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's where the staff of civil protection was quartered, as far as I know, in the firemen's hall where the fire engines were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now at paragraph 13, the mayor says that he went on the local radio station at around 4.00 p.m. and told the people not to panic, that he advised them to stay at home, that the front line was stable, and that if they heard shelling, they should go to a safe location. Now, isn't it true that the meeting you described being present at, didn't take place at 4.00 p.m.; it took place closer to 6.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was 6.00 or not. I believe I will state by what I said, that it was around 4.00 p.m. I wanted to add something. I don't know what local radio station the president had in mind. I did not hear of such a station in Benkovac. There may have been one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, at this meeting, who was it that told that you the final destination was Petrovac in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly cannot recall who was the person from the staff that told me that, but somebody did. The president was there, and then read Draca, aka "Lala" was there. I think he was a member of the Executive Council. As for who told me that exactly, I don't know. I just remember that somebody told me that the final destination was supposed to be Bosansko Grahovo. That was the direction that i sent the first bus to. I assigned the driver to go there and then to come back to evacuate other people as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe you said the destination was supposed to be Bosansko Grahovo. Did you mean to say Bosanski Petrovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pardon me, Bosanski Petrovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have one final matter I would like to pull up on the screen. It is 65 ter 1831.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, the statement you were just referring, to is that the one that of which we denied admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe you did. And if I --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wasn't it because there were objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm -- yes, there are objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And wasn't it that it was -- that you considered that indicia of unreliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Which means that there are specific portions I warranted to put to him. If you read through the statement there is no discussion that I could find about the meeting that the witness talks about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2, this is an interview of Mr. Martic, and it is a Prosecution document from 1996, page 2 in the B/C/S. And if we can scroll down just a little bit there. If we can go to page 3 in the English, please. Can we scroll up in the B/C/S, please. It's the first -- there it is, right there, if we could stop in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This, Mr. President, I'm just -- in preparing for this witness I came across this, and I wanted to make sure to put it in evidence and bar table it if necessary. This is Mr. Martic asked about the events on the 4th of August. He says: "I was in Knin." This is the second paragraph from the bottom, "and to many it looks funny. I dare say everybody knew about the attack except me. I was with my family in my loft where I lived, and I survived that first attack by pure chance because two projectiles passed only a few centimetres away."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we just wanted to tender that and [indiscernible] housekeeping session, if we could ask that this be admitted but again it's on the 65 ter list of the Prosecution. So we tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There is no objection. I think the Chamber had some views on newspaper articles. I don't know if that falls within that ambit or not. We don't objective to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number to it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit D1449.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1449 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, thank you very much for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cayley, still the same position, no questions. Mr. Cayley, still no questions? Mr. Cayley is so busy that ... Still no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. No questions from us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mikulicic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I am, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Mikulicic is counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just looking at the clock. It is five minutes to half past 10.00. I wouldn't be long in my cross-examination, but I don't think I could squeeze it within five minutes, so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you -- Mr. Hedaraly, I'm also looking at you, how many time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Probably five to ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time would you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Let's say 15 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's too much, because the Chamber had in mind to have a bit of a longer break and then have a housekeeping session, but that would be too much before the break. So then we'd rather break -- take the break right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could have some guidance after the break, after the witness's testimony if we will then do the submissions first or the MFI just so that we can have the right people in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then, I have to ... I think we will start with reading out a few decisions which could -- could be postponed. Next on my agenda would be oral reply in relation to interviews of the accused. Then we would briefly deal with D568. And after that, we would deal with adding documents, summarising investigative steps taken by civilian authorities. That is an issue you're aware of. And we would deal with Witness 43. And, finally, at the end, we would deal with the MFI list. That is more or less the sequence I have on my mind at this moment. We will have a break, and we will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Mikulicic, and I think I indicated already that he's counsel for Mr. Markac. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Sinobad. Do you have in front of you a copy of the statement that you gave to the OTP in 2007?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it in front of me, but I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Yes. P2362 is the number, for the transcript. Mr. Sinobad, you said that from 1984 until 1995, you were the manager of the Zagreb transportation company, Zagrebacki Transporti. You said that it was a state-run company; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As for 1995, since in 1990, a holding company was established, then every entity became a legal entity. In Benkovac, it was called Auto Transport Benkovac, and it was registered with commercial court in Split. It was in 1989 or 1990, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That is to say, that at the time -- or, rather, from 1990 until 1995, you were the manager of a part of a company that was registered with the commercial court in Split; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As for the ownership structure of the company, what was it like? Was this a privately opened company or was it something different?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Autotransport d.o.o. Benkovac was how it was registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That's the organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: But I'm interested in the ownership structure. Who owned the company?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The state, or, rather, Zagreb transport or Croatia Transport, or whatever it was called at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: When you say the state, you are referring to the Republic of Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Socially owned enterprise. I mean it was a socially-owned enterprise, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, you said that the company in Benkovac of which you were the director had 20 buses.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, as you've said in your statement, these buses were used for the evacuation of the population of Benkovac and the surrounding area; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: After the evacuation was carried out, what happened with the buses?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain number of buses I never saw again, and I never knew where they were, because the drivers who brought these -- these people took away the buses to the places where these people were staying. Now, was this some kind of collective accommodate or people staying with relative, whatever. At any rate I never saw them again. Some of the buses were in Belgrade and the drivers took them -- I mean, well, they had they had their own private business with these buses afterwards; so I don't think at the moment there is an single one that is still operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Sinobad, about any one of these 20 buses being returned to the owner? That is to say, the state-run company, Zagrebacki Transporti, from the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that not a single one was returned. Perhaps I would allow for the possibility that say one was returned since one of the busses -- one of the bus drivers returned. Cedo Opatic, he now lives in the village of Biocin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, in view of the position you held, were you ever asked about the return of these buses, were any questions every put to you by the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not to me, but I don't see why this question would be put to me since the company itself withered away and the buses left and the bus drivers took them away. They were gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: That is it most certainly correct. But you were the one who organised the transportation with these buses as the director of the company; right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Mikulicic. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Sinobad, I just have a few questions for you based on other questions that you were asked to answer. The first thing I would like to ask you is you remember Mr. Misetic showing you a statement of another witness regarding shells that fell close to the police station in Benkovac; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember these shells falling.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I understand that. Can you tell the Court how many police officers worked in the police station in Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I really don't know. If I needed to have some business of my own done, that's when I went to the police station, like to extend my ID or something like that. I don't even know who the head of the station was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: How large a facility was it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building itself of the police station was quite big. That is to say, there was a ground floor and then upstairs - how should I put this? - there was a space of, say, 200 square metres, or so, if I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were there civilian employees, not police officers, working in that building?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Civilian persons worked there on issuing IDs, passports so these were civilians working for the police. That is to say that there were even women who worked on these jobs, issuing IDs, I mean. So it wasn't done by the police themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On the occasions that you visited building, how many people did you see there?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for the building itself, if we were to exclude the people who worked there, they were mostly operatives. I mean, it wasn't that there were police patrols, so in the building itself, as far as police personnel, there was a maximum of ten persons apart from the civilians I mean who worked there in the services that I have already referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just indicate add maximum of -- of -- what I understood to be police officers. Can you also provide an estimation of how many civilians people worked there as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think it would be around the same figure about ten people worked there, since people worked in shifts on these jobs, issuing IDs, passports, and other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. I now wanted to -- to deal with an issue that was also raised in the course of your cross-examination about the shelling that occurred both before 1995 and that occurred on the 4th of August in 1995 and your reactions to that. Now, if I remember correctly, you testified that between 1992 and 1995, the shelling would last approximately 10 to 15 minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how long did the shelling last on 4 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the detonations could be heard for hours. That is to say, from early morning, when they started, until later. That is to say, went on for several hours. I'm referring to the entire area, the area of the municipality, from which the detonations were coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Between 1992 and 1995, did you also hear detonations in the area of Benkovac but not in the town itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that period, for the most part, I remember that shells fell around the bus station as I've already said in that park. At that time, it was just a meadow. So there was this series of shells that would fall, and then a lull in the shelling, and then a new series, and then they would move. I don't know whether they were guided or not, but at any rate, they were moved in a way because they fell in the vicinity of the bus station, the motor society, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, are you talking between 1992 and 1995; or are you talking about the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Some questions were put to you, Mr. Sinobad, about the buses and whether they were returned or not, and you told us that you had information that you would have been charged or investigated for the disappearance of the buses. utterances.speaker: DUSAN SINOBAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean -- well, I talked to people. I was interested in this. But I believe that there was no legal possibility for charging me for the disappearance of these buses because I was the director of the bus company in Benkovac up until that day. After that day, I was given the assignment of transporting the civilian population with those buses. The drivers drove these civilians to different places: Some went to Belgrade; others to southern Serbia; others to eastern Serbia or Vojvodina. And these drivers thought that they were the owners of the vehicles because on account of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I stop you there. I'm not interested in the details of what happened with the buses but I was, rather, interested in -- in whether any legal action was taken against you, but I do understand from your answers that this was not the case.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was my question for you. I have no further questions. Has the questions in re-examination triggered any need for further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.
